name: NHS & respiratory
summary: UKHSA data to 15 Nov: flu admissions up 24.5% to 4.7 per 100,000 and positivity 11.4%; still below high levels
state: UKHSA's dashboard, updated on 19 Nov, put the influenza hospital admission rate at 4.7 per 100,000 in the week to 15 Nov, up 24.5% on the week, with test positivity rising to 11.4% from 8.0% (UKHSA). Flu is above baseline and rising but not at high levels nationally, and searches on 24 Nov found no widespread NHS critical incidents, so Watch is kept. UKHSA's next weekly report, with data to 22 Nov, is due on 26 Nov (UKHSA).
for_you: Waits in A&E and for hospital beds tend to lengthen as flu rises. The NHS advises using NHS 111 for urgent but non-emergency care, and eligible people can still get a free flu vaccine.
rubric_hit: Watch: UKHSA flu activity above baseline and rising (admissions 4.7/100k, +24.5% to 15 Nov); not high nationally

why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.
drivers: Flu, COVID, RSV, norovirus, staffing, strikes.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.
